title: Dressed Floquet scars from protected zero modes in a Rydberg chain
authors: Saptadip Roy, Bhaskar Mukherjee, K. Sengupta, Arnab Sen
abstract: In this Letter, we present an approximate analytic construction of two zero quasienergy quantum many-body scars in a periodically driven model of Rydberg atoms on a ring, which persist over a range of driving amplitudes and frequencies for finite sizes. An index theorem protects an exponentially large number (in system size) of exact zero energy modes of the Floquet Hamiltonian in this setting. Unlike most of these zero modes which continuously change with drive parameters, these two quantum many-body scars retain the memory of particular states. They can be expressed as {\it dressed versions} of two contrasting states, the Rydberg vacuum and a unitarily rotated variant of a volume-law scar [Ivanov and Motrunich, Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 134}, 050403 (2025)], respectively. We provide an analytic understanding of their existence using a Floquet perturbation theory and show their resilience beyond the perturbative regime using exact diagonalization in finite systems. Our study provides insight into the structure of protected zero modes in interacting Floquet settings.
summary: The paper theoretically constructs and analyzes two robust quantum many-body scars—one related to the vacuum state and another derived from a known scar—in a Rydberg atom chain subjected to periodic driving. By using advanced techniques like Floquet perturbation theory, the authors demonstrate that these scars persist even when the system parameters are varied significantly, providing deep insight into protected zero modes in driven quantum matter.
main_problem: The study investigates protected zero quasienergy quantum many-body scars (QMBSs) arising from symmetry protection in a periodically driven Rydberg atom chain.
main_result: Two distinct QMBSs, corresponding to the Rydberg vacuum and a dressed Ivanov-Motrunich scar, are analytically constructed and shown to persist over significant ranges of driving amplitudes and frequencies.
method: The analysis employs Floquet perturbation theory (FPT) combined with exact diagonalization (ED) on finite systems to analyze the effective Floquet Hamiltonian ($	ext{H}_F$).
model_or_system: The system is a Rydberg atom chain modeled by a time-periodic PXP Hamiltonian on a ring, whose dynamics are governed by the stroboscopic Floquet unitary $U(T, 0)$.
key_observables: Overlap measures ($W_0$), two-point spin correlation functions ($\langle O_{i,j} angle$), and the Loschmidt echo ($L(nT)$) are key diagnostics.
important_parameters: Drive amplitudes ($\lambda$) and frequencies ($\omega_D$ or $T$), which dictate whether the system is in a perturbative or nonperturbative regime.
main_assumptions: The analytic construction of zero modes relies on symmetry protection (index theorem), but the full nullspace itself changes with drive parameters, limiting the description to approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overlap of parent states with Floquet eigenstates, show how correlation functions retain memory effects, and map out the stability regions for the dressed scars as driving parameters are varied.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the theoretical framework using FPT and BCH expansions to derive $	ext{H}_F$, then analyzes specific parent states (vacuum and IM scar) by calculating their overlap with the nullspace of $	ext{H}_F$ across varying driving regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, analytical understanding of how symmetry protection can stabilize non-trivial quantum scars in complex, periodically driven many-body systems, bridging concepts from Floquet engineering and localization theory.
